title: Handbook
content:
Atom keeps related knowledge in a small tree.
Each card should hold one claim or fact.
Place canonical guidance under one topic and link to it from other branches.
Agents can compile a branch when they need its context.

children.title: How to write a card
children.content:
A card states one fact that can be checked on its own.
Use a title that makes the claim in one short sentence.
Put evidence in the body and link to source cards when a claim depends on them.
Split a card when it starts making unrelated claims.

children.title: Where things go
children.content:
Use Projects for work that changes over time.
Use Knowledge for reusable facts and explanations.
Use Agents for instructions shared by agent sessions.
Use References for external sources, one card per source.

title: Projects
content:
Projects collect work with an owner and a current state.
Keep decisions, incidents, and work notes close to the project they describe.
Link shared knowledge instead of copying it.

children.title: Harbor
children.content:
Harbor is a small job queue backed by PostgreSQL.
A fictional payment service and mail service use it to process background work.
The queue stays inside each service database.

children.title: Overview
children.content:
Harbor accepts background jobs from the payment and mail services.
Workers claim jobs, perform one unit of work, and record the outcome.
The system favors simple recovery paths over exactly-once claims.

children.title: Architecture
children.content:
The queue uses ordinary PostgreSQL tables and transactions.
Workers claim jobs in short transactions, then perform work outside the claim transaction.
Shared queue concepts live under Knowledge.

children.title: Retry schedule
children.content:
A failed job waits before it becomes eligible again.
The delay grows with each attempt and includes random jitter.
Cap the delay so an old job does not wait without bound.

children.title: Job states
children.content:
A new job starts as queued and a worker claim moves it to running.
Successful work moves to done.
A retryable error returns it to queued after its delay.
An exhausted job moves to dead for inspection.

children.title: Metrics we export
children.content:
Export queue depth by state and the age of the oldest queued job.
Record claim time, completion time, attempt count, and dead job count.
Avoid high-cardinality labels such as job IDs.

children.title: Decisions
children.content:
Decisions record a choice and its reason.
Keep each decision short and link related technical knowledge.
Replace a decision with a new record when the choice changes.

children.title: ADR-001 Keep the queue in PostgreSQL
children.content:
Context: both services already depend on PostgreSQL.
Decision: store jobs in the service database and claim them with row locks.
This keeps job state close to the data that work changes.
Revisit the choice if measured load outgrows the database.

children.title: ADR-002 At-least-once delivery
children.content:
A worker can finish external work and fail before recording completion.
The queue may then deliver the job again.
Consumers must make repeated requests safe with an idempotency key.
This is an at-least-once contract.

children.title: ADR-003 No separate scheduler process
children.content:
Workers query for queued jobs whose retry time has arrived.
The database clock is the source for eligibility checks.
A separate scheduler would add deployment and recovery work without a current need.

children.title: Incidents
children.content:
Incident cards record what happened and what changed afterward.
Keep the timeline factual and link the decisions that shaped the response.
Use fictional examples in this demo.

children.title: 2026-09-14 Duplicate emails after failover
children.content:
After a database failover, a worker retried a mail job whose send had already succeeded.
The mail service had no idempotency check for that request.
We added a request key and made duplicate delivery return the stored result.
The queue contract remains at-least-once.

children.title: 2026-10-02 Slow dequeue on a bloated table
children.content:
Dequeue time rose as old job rows accumulated in the table.
The active-row index remained small, but dead tuples increased scan work.
We reviewed autovacuum activity and added a table maintenance check.
We also retained completed jobs for a shorter period.

children.title: Work log
children.content:
Short dated notes capture completed changes.
The five newest entries are shown in the normal compiled view.
The journal limit keeps recent notes visible.

children.title: 2026-10-20 Added queue depth alert
children.content:
Added an alert for queued jobs above the service threshold.
The alert includes the oldest queued job age.
The on-call runbook now links to the queue dashboard.

children.title: 2026-10-21 Reduced retry noise
children.content:
Grouped retry logs by job key and attempt number.
Routine retry messages now use the lower log level.
Failures that reach the dead state remain visible as errors.

children.title: 2026-10-22 Added queue age chart
children.content:
Added a chart for the age of the oldest queued job.
The chart is split by service and queue state.
It helps distinguish a backlog from slow individual jobs.

children.title: 2026-10-23 Paused a bad template
children.content:
Paused a mail template that produced invalid output.
Queued jobs were held until the template was corrected.
The worker reported the template version with each failure.

children.title: 2026-10-24 Replayed stalled jobs
children.content:
Replayed a small set of jobs after fixing a worker timeout.
The replay used the original idempotency keys.
We checked the completion count before reopening the queue.

children.title: 2026-10-25 Verified failover behavior
children.content:
Ran a failover exercise against a disposable test database.
A worker resumed claims after reconnecting.
Repeated mail requests returned the saved result.

children.title: Atlas
children.content:
Atlas is a fictional internal documentation site generated from Markdown.
Teams keep source files in a repository and publish the built site from a review branch.
Its search index is built with each release.

children.title: Overview
children.content:
Atlas turns Markdown files into browsable documentation pages.
Authors review changes in source control before publication.
The published site links back to each source file.

children.title: Build pipeline
children.content:
A build checks Markdown links and front matter before rendering pages.
The output is written to a versioned directory.
Publication switches the site to the completed build.

children.title: Search index
children.content:
The build extracts titles, headings, and short text excerpts.
It writes an index alongside the rendered pages.
The browser searches that index without sending each query to a server.

title: Knowledge
content:
Knowledge cards explain ideas that can help more than one project.
Keep the claim separate from project-specific decisions.
Link from a project to the canonical explanation.

children.title: Databases
children.content:
Database cards describe query patterns and maintenance concepts.
Each card covers one technique or behavior.
External references are kept in References.

children.title: SKIP LOCKED for job queues
children.content:
Workers can select eligible rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
A worker skips rows already locked by another transaction instead of waiting for them.
Use a stable order and update the claimed rows inside the same short transaction.
This pattern allows several workers to claim separate jobs concurrently.

children.title: Partial indexes for hot rows
children.content:
A partial index stores entries only for rows that meet its predicate.
For a queue, an index can cover rows that are still eligible for work.
Keep the query predicate aligned with the index predicate.
Check the plan against real table sizes before adding the index.

children.title: Advisory locks
children.content:
An advisory lock coordinates work that has no natural row to lock.
The application chooses a numeric key and releases the lock according to its scope.
Document the key mapping so separate features do not claim the same lock.
Prefer row locks when a row already represents the resource.

children.title: VACUUM and table bloat
children.content:
PostgreSQL keeps old row versions until they are no longer visible to active transactions.
VACUUM makes dead tuple space reusable and updates visibility information.
Long transactions can prevent cleanup and let tables grow.
Watch dead tuples and autovacuum progress before changing settings.

children.title: Distributed systems
children.content:
These cards describe behavior across retries, processes, and service boundaries.
They focus on guarantees callers can observe.
Use a project decision for the choice made by one system.

children.title: Idempotency keys
children.content:
An idempotency key identifies one logical request across retries.
The service stores the result for a key and returns it when the same request is repeated.
Scope keys to the operation and retain them for the retry window.
Reject reuse of a key with a different request body.

children.title: Backoff with jitter
children.content:
Exponential backoff increases the delay after each failed attempt.
Jitter adds random variation so many clients do not retry together.
Set a maximum delay and an overall retry limit.
Use the same policy for one class of retrying work.

children.title: At-least-once vs exactly-once
children.content:
At-least-once delivery may repeat a message when completion is uncertain.
Exactly-once effects require coordination across delivery and the external side effect.
Most services use retries with idempotent handling instead of claiming a global exactly-once guarantee.
State the boundary of the guarantee.

children.title: Writing
children.content:
Writing cards record reusable conventions for technical knowledge.
Keep examples short and focused.
Link agent instructions here when they need the same guidance.

children.title: Writing instructions for agents
children.content:
Write one claim per card and use a title that states the claim.
Prefer short sentences and familiar technical terms.
Include evidence or a link when the reader needs to verify a fact.
Remove details that do not help the reader act or understand.

children.title: Commit messages
children.content:
Start with a short verb phrase that names the change.
Keep the first line focused on one outcome.
Add a body only when the reason or tradeoff needs context.
Do not repeat the diff in prose.

title: Agents
content:
Agent context is compiled from instructions and shared knowledge.
Keep shared rules short enough to use during a task.
Link to the canonical writing guidance instead of duplicating it.

children.title: Shared rules
children.content:
Shared rules apply across agent roles.
Compile this branch when an agent needs the common task context.
Role-specific checklists stay in their own branches.

children.title: Verify before reporting done
children.content:
Run the smallest command that proves the requested result.
Use fresh output from the final working tree.
Report what was checked and what remains unverified.

children.title: Cite card ids in reports
children.content:
Include a card id when a report refers to a specific card.
Use the id returned by the card system.
Do not guess ids from a title or path.

children.title: Reviewer
children.content:
Reviewer guidance focuses on the user-visible result and the changed code.
Record evidence for each finding.
Keep unrelated issues separate from the current review.

children.title: Review checklist
children.content:
Check the changed behavior against the request.
Trace important values through their callers and storage.
Look for a simpler implementation that preserves the contract.
Report findings with file, line, impact, and a concrete fix.

children.title: Release bot
children.content:
The release bot prepares a versioned build from a reviewed change.
It checks the target branch and reports the artifact location.
A human owns the final release decision.

children.title: Release steps
children.content:
Confirm the requested version and target branch.
Build from the reviewed commit and record its checksum.
Publish the artifact and verify the release page.
Report the commit, artifact, and verification result.

title: References
content:
Each reference card represents one external source.
Record the source URL and the small set of ideas used by this knowledge base.
Keep summaries in your own words.

children.title: PostgreSQL docs: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
children.content:
Workers can skip rows locked by other transactions while claiming work.
Use a short transaction and a consistent ordering for the claim query.
The lock does not replace the need to handle a worker crash after the claim.

children.title: PostgreSQL docs: Routine vacuuming
children.content:
Routine vacuuming makes space from dead rows reusable and maintains visibility information.
Autovacuum normally handles this work.
Long-running transactions can delay cleanup.

children.title: AWS Blog: Exponential Backoff And Jitter
children.content:
Exponential backoff spreads retries over increasing delays.
Jitter randomizes delays so clients do not retry at the same instant.
A retry cap bounds the wait before another attempt.

children.title: Stripe docs: Idempotent requests
children.content:
A client can attach an idempotency key to a request that may be retried.
The service returns a saved result for a repeated matching request.
The caller should keep the key scope and lifetime clear.
